shared.description: Core server infrastructure — database, HTTP routing, utilities, entry point, event bus
shared.rationale: Every server module depends on the DB, router, util helpers, entry-point registration, or the event bus. The UI smoke tests run against the real server binary, so a change here can break any module's backend tests AND its smoke assertions. No part restriction.
Dependency or build-config changes can break any module silently — both compiled server code and the web bundle. Affects both backend and UI.
Every backend test imports from fixtures.ts. fake-sdk and fake-kiro are used across multiple test suites. These are test helpers only — they don't affect the built server or the smoke suite.
The smoke runner itself is shared UI infrastructure. Changes to timing, helpers, section list, or the SMOKE_ONLY mechanism only affect smoke (UI) outcomes, not backend unit tests.

The agent runner executes sessions, drives workflow steps, runs code reviews, branch scans, and test runs. browser-headless.ts rewrites Playwright MCP entries; browser-manager.ts provides the per-session live browser. Server code — affects both backend tests and smoke (via running server behaviour). No part restriction.

shared.description: Core web app infrastructure — routing, API client, event system, global styles
shared.rationale: Every page is rendered through App.jsx and uses api.js, events, and the global stylesheet. Web-only files — they don't affect backend unit tests. Affects only UI parts.

shared.description: Universal UI primitives — icons, skeleton loading, toast notifications
shared.rationale: Used on virtually every page; a breakage is visible across the entire UI. Web-only files — affects only UI parts.
